meta.title: EduFlow · Test papers, lesson plans and course syllabi with an AI assistant
meta.description: Desktop app for macOS and Windows: test papers, lesson plans, course syllabi and degree program review, with an AI assistant and your data on your computer.

hero.eyebrow: Desktop app for macOS and Windows
hero.h1: Write test papers, lesson plans and course syllabi, and review degree programs, with one AI assistant
hero.sub: Chat with the assistant right beside the screen you are working on. The app builds the standard structure, AI fills in the content, and you review and sign.
hero.platformNote: EduFlow runs on macOS and Windows computers.
hero.trust1: Your data stays on your computer
hero.imageAlt: EduFlow home screen: the chat column with the assistant and a preview of the test paper about to be created

levels.h2: A workspace for every role, one way of working
levels.lead: K-12 teachers, lecturers and the Quality Assurance Office share one app. All three levels are open to everyone, with nothing locked behind a plan.

assistant.h2: Ask, request edits and hand over tasks right on the screen you are working on
assistant.lead: The assistant understands the project and artifact you have open, answers in three tiers of conclusions and offers action cards, so the app does the work when you click.

p1.title: Knows what you are looking at
p1.desc: The “Viewing” chips show each item that is sent. The assistant only receives a structured summary, never the original files; remove a chip and that item is not sent.

p2.title: Local actions cost nothing, AI tasks quote first
p2.desc: Cards like running a gate, recompiling or opening the right screen run directly on your computer. AI tasks always show a cost range before they run.

p3.title: Suggests edits, you decide
p3.desc: The assistant shows changes as before and after. Applying one creates a new draft; a signed version is never modified.

p4.title: Never approves or signs on your behalf
p4.desc: The Approve and Sign buttons live only on the main screen. Ask the assistant to sign and it lists the missing conditions and opens the right screen for you.

assistant.imageAlt: Test paper results screen with the assistant panel explaining gate P5 and suggesting a fix to one answer option

pipeline.h2: Five steps, with a person deciding at the last one
pipeline.caption: Every step leaves a trail: who did it, when, and against which standard.

s1.title: Set up
s1.desc: Choose the standards framework, subject, course or degree program records. You can start with a single sentence to the assistant.

s2.title: AI fills in structured content
s2.desc: The app builds a fixed structure; AI only fills in the content under a strict data contract.

s3.title: Quality gates check
s3.desc: Each gate prints how many units it checked. A gate that checked 0 units counts as an error and never reports a pass.

s4.title: You review and sign
s4.desc: AI content carries the Suggestion label until it is approved. Signing locks the version, and its hash is notarized.

s5.title: Export and share
s5.desc: Export PDF, DOCX, PPTX or a signed package for the head of subject group, the head of department or the Quality Assurance Office.

t1.title: Your data stays on your computer
t1.desc: Projects, artifacts and chat history stay on your computer. The server only relays content to the model and records token counts; it never stores content.

t2.title: Three tiers of conclusions, never mixed
t2.desc: The deterministic tier states facts with their basis. The comparative tier says “not found yet” with the number checked. The suggestion tier always needs human review.

t3.title: Checking 0 units does not mean clean
t3.desc: Every quality gate prints how many units it checked; a gate that checked nothing counts as an error.

t4.title: Signatures and hash notarization
t4.desc: Signed versions are locked against edits. The server notarizes the hash without seeing the content, and package recipients can verify it.

t5.title: Works offline
t5.desc: Quality gates, recompiling, signing and exporting files keep working offline. Only the AI parts need a connection.

t6.title: Transparent costs
t6.desc: Every AI task shows an estimated cost before it runs and the actual cost after it runs.

cost.h2: Pay for the AI you use; what runs on your computer is free
cost.body: EduFlow charges by the AI tokens used. Quality gates, test version shuffling, compiling and “what if” scenarios run on your computer at no cost. Each key has a monthly budget and warns you at 80% usage.

prelaunch.body: Installers for macOS and Windows will be available here at release. Schools that want early access can contact Agentra.

q1.q: What is a license key and where do I get one?
q1.a: Each school, faculty or individual receives one license key for an agreed number of computers. Send a request right in the app or contact Agentra to get a key.

q2.a: Download and open EduFlow, click Try it on the first screen and fill in the form. A trial key works on 1 computer, with a trial budget and an expiry date.

q3.q: Do I need an Internet connection?
q3.a: Yes, to activate, to run AI tasks and to ask the assistant. Quality gates, recompiling, signing and exporting files keep working offline.

q4.q: Where is my data stored, and what does the assistant send?
q4.a: Projects and artifacts stay on your computer. The assistant only sends a structured summary of the open screen, never the original files. The server does not store content.

q5.a: By the AI tokens used, with a monthly budget per key. What runs on your computer is free. Details are on the Pricing page; schools can contact Agentra for a quote.

q6.q: How many computers can one key be used on?
q6.a: As many as the number of devices on your organization's key. When you change computers, an Agentra administrator revokes the old one to free a slot for the new one.

q7.q: Can a school turn off AI for a project?
q7.a: Yes. Switch AI off in the project details and the app sends no AI calls for that project, including the assistant; everything that runs on your computer keeps working as usual.

q8.q: How do I update to a new version?
q8.a: The app tells you when a new version is available. Click Download, then Restart to install; your projects and data stay as they are.

cta.sub: Download the app to try it, or contact Agentra for a quote based on the size of your school.

meta.title: K-12 level: test papers, lesson plans, slides
meta.description: Four-level test blueprints and multiple test versions, Official Letter 5512 (CV5512) lesson plans, quiz slides, 12 quality gates, sign-off before publishing.

hero.h1: Test papers, lesson plans and slides for every lesson
hero.lead: Choose the curriculum framework, build the test blueprint, let AI fill in the content, then review each warning yourself before publishing.
hero.audience: For K-12 teachers, heads of subject groups and school leadership.
hero.note: Exports carry the TRIAL (DÙNG THỬ) watermark until you sign.

outcomes.h2: From test blueprint to a full test set with appendices

o1.title: Test papers from a four-level test blueprint
o1.desc: A test blueprint of recall, understanding, application and advanced application by topic; the question count per level is the source of truth.

o2.title: Multiple test versions, deterministic shuffling
o2.desc: Each test version shuffles question and option order with a fixed seed and comes with a specification table, answer key and marking guide.

o3.title: Independent answer check
o3.desc: A separate AI pass solves the test again. Any question whose answer changes becomes a warning, and you confirm each one.

o4.title: Lesson plans per Official Letter 5512 (CV5512)
o4.desc: Period-by-period lesson plans with an implementation table, teacher notes and your school's header.

o5.title: Slides with quizzes
o5.desc: Decks follow the required layout, with quizzes spread through the lesson and a preview from the very first step.

o6.title: Full sets and a template library
o6.desc: One setup for the slides, lesson plan and test paper of the same lesson; the template library works offline.

s1.title: Test paper setup
s1.desc: Test blueprint, standards framework and cost estimate on a single screen.

s2.title: Results and 12 gates
s2.desc: The P1..P12 gate table prints how many units were checked; answer warnings must be confirmed question by question.

outcomes.h2: Every element traces back to CLOs and standards

o1.title: CLOs by Bloom level
o1.desc: A CLO set with every field of the standard template and verbs that match the Bloom level; gate G3 catches level mismatches.

o2.title: Weekly plan and LLOs
o2.desc: Each week carries its LLOs, Bloom level, linked CLOs and AI level; the weeks run continuously, with no gaps.

o3.title: 90- or 150-minute session plans
o3.desc: A phase table with lecturer activities, student activities and checks; total minutes match the session length.

o5.title: Assessments with AI levels

o6.title: 10-section course syllabus

screens.h2: Every violation leads straight to what needs fixing

s1.title: Workbench
s1.desc: CLOs, the weekly plan and sessions on one screen, each with its related gates.

s2.title: 12 gates, G1..G12
s2.desc: Violations are sorted by severity, and each one opens exactly what needs fixing and the source standard.

s3.title: Approve, sign and export
s3.desc: The signing checklist, hash notarization and the package sent to the head of department for approval.

gates.title: 12 gates, G1..G12
gates.body: Gates check inputs, CLO fields, Bloom levels, weekly traceability, assessment weights, AI resistance, timing, figures backed by a basis and the approval signature.

meta.title: Degree program level: digital twin, three-tier review
meta.description: Build your degree program's digital twin, check legal validity at a review date and run seven curriculum map checks, a criteria overlay and what-if scenarios.

hero.h1: A digital twin of your degree program, checked at a review date
hero.lead: Load the degree program records and the course syllabus package, build a graph with the provenance of every edge, then review in three tiers: deterministic, comparative, suggestion.
hero.audience: For the Quality Assurance Office, the Program Council and school leadership.
hero.note: This is an internal working document, not a self-assessment report.

outcomes.h2: Conclusions with a basis, no guessing

o1.title: A digital twin with provenance
o1.desc: Every node and edge of the graph records its file, page and line; unknown codes must be confirmed by a person before the graph is built.

o2.title: Legal validity at the review date
o2.desc: Dead basis, expiring basis and not yet in force are three separate counts, never added into one.

o3.title: Seven curriculum map checks
o3.desc: PLO coverage, PI coverage, progression, 5T, overload, gap, duplication; each check prints how many units it checked.

o4.title: Criteria overlay
o4.desc: Each criterion under Circular 04/2025 has exactly one status: evidenced, evidence expired or not found yet.

o5.title: Suggestions need human review
o5.desc: Tier 3 shows suggestions with a dashed border; only approved suggestions go into the report.

o6.title: “What if” scenarios
o6.desc: Try removing a course or changing a PLO on a copy of the graph and see the effect spread to the criteria before making the real change.

s1.title: Digital twin
s1.desc: A layered graph, the provenance of every edge and bridges placed by people.

s2.title: Three-tier review
s2.desc: The review date bar and the tier 1, tier 2 and tier 3 blocks; every number opens a list when clicked.

s3.title: What-if scenario
s3.desc: A before and after table with the spread drawn on the graph, run on your computer at no cost.

gates.title: 12 gates, K1..K12
gates.body: Gates check edge provenance, unknown codes, the review date on every result, all seven checks and the prerequisite criteria before the report is signed.
gates.rule: A gate that checked 0 units shows Gate error, never Pass.

cta.h2: Review your degree program on a clear basis
cta.sub: Download the app and click Try it on the first screen.

how.h2: Clear about what the assistant knows and what it may do

c1.title: Knows what you are looking at
c1.desc: The “Viewing” chips list each context item. Only a structured summary is sent; remove a chip and that item is not sent.

c2.title: Answers in three tiers
c2.desc: Tier 1 blocks only quote the app's deterministic results, in the app's own words. Tier 2 says “not found yet”. Tier 3 is a suggestion that needs human review. Every citation opens its source.

c3.title: Action cards
c3.desc: Local actions such as opening a screen, running a gate, recompiling or running a what-if scenario cost nothing and run when you click. AI tasks open a cost estimate first.

c4.title: Suggested edits go into a draft
c4.desc: Changes appear as before and after. Applying one creates a new draft version and reruns the affected gates.

how.imageAlt: The assistant panel explaining a P5 violation and suggesting a fix to one answer option

never.lead: These actions exist only on the main screen, and you click them yourself.
never.n3: Confirm answer warnings or gate warnings

cost.title: Cost per message
cost.body: The message box shows the cost range per message. Every answer shows its actual cost and token count. Clicking Stop still charges for the part already answered.

states.h2: The assistant says why, and local work keeps running
states.lead: Messages are never silently queued; you know right away what you can still do.
states.imageAlt: Four states of the assistant panel: offline, AI off, key locked, over budget

s1.title: Offline
s1.desc: The message box is locked; local commands typed with / still run.

s2.title: Project has AI off
s2.desc: Nothing leaves your computer for that project.

s3.title: Key locked
s3.desc: The assistant stops while features that do not use AI keep working; a button lets you ask for the key to be reissued.

s4.title: Over budget
s4.desc: In block mode, the assistant stops until next month or until the budget is raised; a button lets you request a higher budget.

privacy.title: Chat history stays on your computer
privacy.body: Conversations are saved per project on your computer and can be deleted at any time. The server does not store chat content; packages sent to colleagues do not carry the history.

meta.title: How pricing works
meta.description: EduFlow charges by the AI tokens used, with a monthly budget per key and costs shown before anything runs; local work is free. Contact Agentra for a quote.

hero.h1: Pay for the AI you use, and know the cost before it runs
hero.lead: EduFlow is not sold in feature plans. All three levels are open to everyone; costs come from AI calls and are always shown before they run.

s1.title: One key per organization
s1.body: Each school, faculty or individual receives one key for an agreed number of computers.

s2.title: Try it in the app
s2.body: Click Try it on the first screen. A trial key works on 1 computer, with a trial budget and an expiry date.

s3.title: Measured in tokens
s3.body: Every AI call measures four token classes: input, output, cache write, cache read. Each class has its own unit price per model.

s4.title: Locked in when recorded
s4.body: The amount for each call is locked in when it is recorded, at the current price list; a new price list only applies to later calls.

s5.title: Know before it runs
s5.body: Every AI task shows an estimated range before it runs and the actual cost after it runs. Assistant messages show the cost under each answer.

s6.title: Monthly budget per key
s6.body: Your organization chooses warn mode or block mode. The app notifies you at 80% and 100% of the budget.

s7.title: Monthly reconciliation
s7.body: Agentra sends a monthly statement per organization as CSV and PDF. The statement is for reconciliation and is not an invoice.

formula.title: The formula for one AI step
formula.expr: Cost = sum over classes (tokens in the class × class unit price) ÷ 1,000,000
formula.note: Unit prices are in VND per million tokens, by model and token class. This page does not publish unit prices; schools receive a quote from Agentra.

budget.h2: Three states of the monthly budget

near.title: Near the limit
near.desc: From 80% of the budget, the app notifies you once on the home screen and in the estimate dialog.

over.title: Over budget
over.desc: Warn mode: tasks keep running. Block mode: AI tasks stop until the 1st of next month or until the budget is raised.

budget.essential: When blocked, OCR of scanned pages and LaTeX compile-error fixes still run, so your exports never get stuck.

meta.title: AI and data transparency
meta.description: Where EduFlow uses AI, what data it sends, which data never leaves your computer, and the principle that the machine suggests and people decide.

transparency.lead: This page matches the AI transparency page in the app: which skills use AI, what data is sent and which data never leaves your computer.

p1.title: Where AI is used
p1.body: AI fills in structured content for test papers, answer rechecks, lesson plans, slides, CLOs, weekly plans, session plans, course syllabi, assessment briefs, tier 3 suggestions in degree program review and the chat assistant. Everything else runs on your computer.

p2.title: Model tiers
p2.body: Each skill runs on the fast, standard or strong tier. Agentra maps each tier to a specific model; the AI transparency page in the app lists the tier of every skill.

p3.title: Data sent out
p3.body: Each call sends only the content the skill needs, under a strict data contract. The assistant sends a structured summary of the open screen with the latest messages of the conversation, never the original files.

p4.title: Data that stays on your computer
p4.body: The project store, chat history, signatures and activation secrets stay on your computer. Imported files are parsed locally; only when you run OCR on a scanned page is that page image sent for text recognition.

p5.title: The server stores no content
p5.body: The server relays content to the model and records token counts, amounts and hashes. Content is neither stored nor written to logs.

p6.title: The machine suggests, people decide
p6.body: AI content carries the Suggestion label until you approve it. There is no button to skip a quality gate; the assistant does not approve or sign.

p7.title: Three tiers of conclusions
p7.body: The deterministic tier states facts with their basis and review date. The comparative tier says “not found yet” with the number of units checked. The suggestion tier opens with “Suggestion, needs human review”.

p8.title: AI off per project
p8.body: Switch AI off in the project details and the app sends no AI calls for that project, including the assistant.
